meaning: Trigger means a requested object/action sound, not a guaranteed ASMR response or a prerecorded clip.
priority: Tongue–saliva/artificial-ear interaction first; other SFX are research inventory only.

sources.title: Original research brief and handoff
sources.support: Requested target and acceptance contract, not experimental evidence.

sources.title: Acoustic emission measurement of rubbing and tapping contacts of skin and tongue surfaces (2013)
sources.support: Records tongue/palate and skin contact acoustics; not tongue on a KU100 ear. Abstract inspected; raw trials not acquired.

sources.title: Negative intraoral pressure in German: Evidence from an exploratory study (2013)
sources.support: Measured negative oral pressure with some clicks; clicks need not establish a simple dual-closure mechanism. Not ASMR calibration.

sources.title: Age-dependent capillary thinning of salivary mucin networks (2017)
sources.support: Shear viscosity alone does not characterize salivary thread lifetime; sample history matters. No ear audio in this source.

sources.title: Acoustic sensing of forces driving fast capillary flows (2020)
sources.support: Microphone-array experiment on bursting soap films. Evidence for capillary acoustic emission in that apparatus, not proof of saliva bubbles in these recordings.

sources.title: Toward animating water with complex acoustic bubbles (2016)
sources.support: Shape/geometry and entrainment matter for water-bubble sound. Does not authorize random bubble pops for saliva.

sources.title: Crumpling sound synthesis (2016)
sources.support: Buckling events and shell dynamics support paper/foil model research; a different source mechanism.

sources.title: EPIC-Sounds: actions that sound
sources.support: Audio event labels plus visually checked collision materials. Useful annotation organization; no calibrated KU100 transfer.

sources.title: YouTube-ASMR-300K
sources.support: The release contains URL lists, not 900 hours of downloadable cleared audio. Spatial-reference lead only; individual recording rights remain separate.

sources.title: FSD50K
sources.support: Human-labeled sound-event audio and per-clip Creative Commons metadata; not paired contact force data. No clips downloaded in this update.

sources.title: Universal Category System
sources.support: SFX library classification vocabulary, not physical equations or a sample playback architecture.

sources.title: Passive tube models with viscothermal losses (2016)
sources.support: Basis for passive tube methods; implemented viscous component is separately checked. Thermal admittance is absent.

items.listen_for: Sustained wet texture and direction changes tied to contact, not stationary filtered noise.
items.state: Position, normal/tangential load, real contact area, liquid supply, prior contact.
items.gap: Source location and calibrated force-to-both-ears relationship not established.

items.listen_for: Changing contact patch and continuous, nonrepeating texture.
items.state: Orientation, patch migration, deformation and liquid history.
items.gap: No tongue/ear geometry or dynamic contact data fitted; a fixed plate footprint is not rolling.

items.listen_for: Event structure and decay during separation; audible descriptors do not identify a bubble or adhesive mechanism.
items.state: Separation speed, wetting, thread extension and contact-line behavior.
items.gap: No measured target release law. Pressure-release probe tests only one alternative source.

items.listen_for: Does a discrete air-pressure release resemble a short target transient? Compare fast opening, slow opening and never-sealed control.
items.state: Pocket pressure, neck flow and viscous/radiation memory. Geometry is assumed, not fitted.
items.gap: Not saliva mechanics, not a tongue-to-ear contact path; target mechanism remains unidentified.

items.listen_for: Distinguish an airborne mouth source from direct ear contact before selecting a solver.
items.state: Articulation, local contact and oral pressure; not inferable from loudness alone.
items.gap: Supplied avatar-derived reference has no measured contact video.

items.listen_for: Soft broadband fiber friction and discrete contact changes.
items.state: Fiber contact, pressure, speed, placement and local transmission.
items.gap: No generated swab source or device-specific calibration in this update.

items.object: Soft brush / hair or artificial ear
items.listen_for: Distributed bristle contact rather than one repeated sample.
items.state: Bristle dynamics, material, pressure and path.

items.object: Nail or tool / glass, wood, metal
items.listen_for: Material resonances, impact attack and scrape microcontacts.
items.state: Impact location/velocity, geometry, support and radiation.
items.gap: A generic plate cannot automatically represent every item.

items.listen_for: Buckling-event clusters and material-specific transient structure.
items.state: Shell deformation, bending and buckling events.
items.gap: Independent shell problem; no paper samples or synthesis shipped.

items.listen_for: Film/bubble events if supported by imaging—not any arbitrary pop library.
items.state: Film geometry, surface stresses, entrainment and boundary conditions.
items.gap: Soap/water results are not saliva-on-ear validation.

items.listen_for: Lubricated contact texture distinct from saliva and foam.
items.state: Liquid rheology, surface condition, pressure and speed.
items.gap: Oil cannot be represented by renaming the wetness slider.

items.listen_for: Separate opposite-channel handling sounds from tongue/ear reference events.
items.state: Object material, deformation and side of microphone.
items.gap: Some original chapter intervals mix actions; do not use them as isolated wet-ear targets.
